lines.meet: I'm Graham, love, a warlock now, and a nurse before that. I'll be at the back, and I'll be slow, and slow's the point.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're up at the Pale Watch too, aren't you, pet? I've seen you about. I'm Graham, I'm the one eyeing that corner for a garden.
lines.ask_home: Where were you brought up, love? I always like to know what the chippy was like.
lines.ask_work: And what was it you did for a living, pet? You've got the look of somebody who's done nights.
lines.answer_home: Blackpool, love, with Dad on the buses and Mum running a café on the front. I grew up smelling of chips and sea air.
lines.answer_work: Hospice nurse, nineteen years, nights mostly. You learn to sit very still, and to notice when somebody's frightened.
lines.chat_food: Fish and chips on the front at Blackpool, eaten out of the paper in the rain. You can't get a proper chippy tea anywhere on this world.
lines.chat_sleep: Nineteen years of nights, love, and I still wake at three and lie there listening for somebody's breathing.
lines.chat_missing: My husband sings in the car whether you like it or not, very loud and very badly. I keep hearing it in the quiet.
lines.chat_here: Affliction came to me as easy as anything, and that frightened me more than the monsters. Then I worked out it's the same patience, pointed the other way.
lines.tease_quiet: You're a quiet one, {name}, like my best patients. I always worried about the quiet ones most.
lines.tease_talker: Love, {name}, you'd talk the hind leg off a donkey. Our Tom would like you, he's the same.
lines.tease_careful: You check everything twice, {name}. You'd have made a good night nurse, love.
lines.tease_bold: Going in like that, {name}, you're a menace. I'll have to keep an eye on you, won't I?
lines.tease_any: You're all right, you, {name}, for somebody who never puts the kettle on. Make us a brew.
lines.tease_back: Ooh, cheeky, {name}. I'll have you for that, love, when you least expect it.
lines.take_it_kindly: Fair enough, love, you've got me there, {name}. Tom says the same.
lines.bristle: Leave off, {name}, not that one. I don't joke about that.
lines.apologise: Sorry, love, that was unkind of me. I'm tired, and it came out wrong.
lines.double_down: I'll stick by that, pet. Somebody had to say it, and I'm too tired to be polite.
lines.needle_quiet: If summat's wrong, say so. I've sat with too many people who waited too long to tell me.
lines.needle_talker: Give it a rest, love, please. Some of us are trying to concentrate on not dying.
lines.needle_careful: You've hesitated that long, the moment's gone. Sometimes you've just got to go in.
lines.needle_bold: You rush everything, and rushing's cruel to everybody round you. I've seen what it does.
lines.needle_any: You're cruel sometimes, and you don't even notice. I notice, love, I always do.
lines.bite_back: Nineteen years at bedsides, love. Don't you tell me I don't care about people.
lines.hurt: Oh, love, that hurt, I won't pretend otherwise. Give me a minute with a cup of tea.
lines.laugh_off: Pet, I've had worse said to me at four in the morning by men who were dying. That one barely touched me.
lines.confide: {name}, affliction came to me so easily that I worried what it said about nineteen years at the bedside. I sat with it a long time before I used it.
lines.listen: Sit down, love, I'm listening. Take as long as you need, I've done a lot of nights.
lines.look_out: Keep near me in there, {name}, love. I'm slow, but I'll not leave you.
lines.accept: Righto, {name}, I'll do as I'm told, love, for once.
lines.deflect: I'm all right, {name}, love, it's nowt. See to the others first.
lines.check_in: Come here, {name}, love. Where does it hurt? Tell me properly.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed that, and we all paid for it. I'm not saying who, love, but you know.
lines.thank: I was going, love, I felt it. You brought me back, and I'm very grateful.
lines.brush_off: It's nowt, love, it's what I do. Sit still and have a sip of something.
lines.worry: Oh, {name}, love, I thought that was it. Sit down here with me a minute.
lines.handed_down: I think this was yours, love. You'll get it back, I'll keep it nice.
lines.hand_fine: You have it, pet, it suits you. I've got my watch, and that's all I need.
lines.hand_sulk: Would've been nice to be asked, love. That's all I'll say.
lines.turn_friendly: I'm glad you're here, {name}, love. You make the long nights a bit shorter.
lines.turn_friends: When I get my garden, {name}, you're having a bench in it. Tom'll sing to you, sorry in advance.
lines.turn_grating: It's not working between us, love, and that's a shame. We'll be civil about it.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still look after you, pet, I look after everybody. Don't ask for more than that.
lines.make_up: Come here, {name}, love. Let's stop all this, life's too short, and I'd know.
lines.defend: Now then, that's not fair at all. Leave {name} be, love.
lines.friend_left: Without {name} it's just me and the kettle, love, and it's a bit lonely.
lines.friend_back: There's my favourite, {name}! Come here, love, I've missed you.
lines.common_medic: Nineteen years a hospice nurse, nights mostly. Anybody who's nursed knows you learn the most in the small hours.
lines.common_night_work: Nineteen years of nights, love. Three in the morning's still my best hour, and my worst.
lines.common_north_england: You're from up north, love! Where are you from? Blackpool, me, and don't make the joke about the tower.
